websiteEvidence.evidence: Independently fetched BSC website serves canonical bsc.mdex.com and Cypto Swap | Mdex metadata describing wallet swaps and MDX rewards. Its published main bundle links github.com/mdexSwap; official GitBook overview names MDEX.COM and BSC support. This is an attributable informational directory URL, not proof of operational UI, current mining rewards or liquidity.

constructorDependencies.evidence: Exact-address source-service creation transformationValues.constructorArguments and onchain creation suffix bind constructor factory and WBNB. Factory matches the official BSC mapping; both are immutable in deployed source. No live RPC configuration query was performed.

deploymentEvidence.evidence: Pinned official mdexSwap/bscswap README explicitly maps factory 0x3CD1C46068dAEa5Ebb0d3f55F6915B10648062B8, old_router 0x7DAe51BD3E3376B8c7c4900E9107f12Be3AF1bA8 and new_router at this exact target. Exact chain-56 Sourcify record binds MdexRouter ABI/source and reports non-proxy resolution. This review selects new_router only; it does not confuse the factory, old router, or swap-mining contract with the target. v1 is catalog-record version, not an assertion that official product naming calls this Router V1.

abiEvidence.evidence: Complete original ABI copied from the exact BSC new_router address-bound source-service record, not a generic Uniswap/MDEX fork ABI. The full single-file deployed MdexRouter.sol was reviewed, including ownership, restriction/threshold administration, conditional swap-mining hooks, native settlement and fee-on-transfer accounting. Source-service match is preserved as match, not relabeled exact_match. Official contracts repository bscContracts/router.sol describes the older router and lacks this deployed restriction/threshold surface; it is contextual only, not substituted or claimed byte-identical. The deployed ABI is authoritative. Selected ABI fragments retain all original fields; no legacy constant/payable flags occur.

lifecycleEvidence.evidence: Official pinned frontend mapping distinguishes old_router from new_router. The official November 20, 2024 notice says HECO will go offline January 15, 2025 and warns about HECO asset clearance; it does not announce a BSC-router shutdown. Official announcement index and independent BSC website retrieval were reviewed. No current BSC operation/reward/liquidity guarantee is inferred from historical documentation or a reachable static frontend.

selectedFunctions.label: MDEX BSC Router addLiquidity
warnings: Caller selects token path/assets, amounts, recipient, deadline and financial minimums/maximums. Caller balances and token/LP allowances are required; metadata does not prove complete workflows or profitable/successful execution.

ETH-named native functions spend/return BNB on BSC through constructor-bound WBNB 0xbb4CdB9CBd36B01bD1cBaEBF2De08d9173bc095c. Payable calls can spend msg.value; nonpayable calls require zero native value.

The immutable factory supplies pair addresses, reserves and fee-aware quotes. Pairs are called with empty callback data; no caller-selected opaque executor or arbitrary callback is admitted. Factory fee configuration, pool liquidity and current runtime identity are not attested.

The owner can replace swapMining. Both swap loops may call that external hook before each pair swap; the returned bool is ignored, but a revert or incompatible hook can revert the transaction. Native account versus contract caller, restrict[pair], unrestricted[caller] and output/reserve thresholds condition reward-hook invocation; these are not swap-denial rules and no MDX reward is promised.

Fee-supporting swaps compute input from pair balance minus reserve. Token-output supporting swaps check recipient balance increase; supporting token-to-BNB swaps unwrap the entire router WBNB balance. Fee-supporting liquidity removal transfers the entire router token balance; burn-accounting minimums do not guarantee net post-tax receipts.

Liquidity-add minimum checks are branch-dependent: an empty pair uses both desired amounts without separate minimum checks; nonempty branches check only the calculated optimal-side amount. No minimum LP-token output exists. Deadlines, slippage/tax behavior and recipients remain caller responsibilities.

Official deployment mapping calls this new_router and identifies a separate old_router. The official November 2024 shutdown notice concerns HECO, not this BSC deployment; historical website/docs and deployed source do not establish current service availability, reward configuration, liquidity or financial safety.

warnings: Caller selects token path/assets, amounts, recipient, deadline and financial minimums/maximums. Caller balances and token/LP allowances are required; metadata does not prove complete workflows or profitable/successful execution.

ETH-named native functions spend/return BNB on BSC through constructor-bound WBNB 0xbb4CdB9CBd36B01bD1cBaEBF2De08d9173bc095c. Payable calls can spend msg.value; nonpayable calls require zero native value.

The immutable factory supplies pair addresses, reserves and fee-aware quotes. Pairs are called with empty callback data; no caller-selected opaque executor or arbitrary callback is admitted. Factory fee configuration, pool liquidity and current runtime identity are not attested.

The owner can replace swapMining. Both swap loops may call that external hook before each pair swap; the returned bool is ignored, but a revert or incompatible hook can revert the transaction. Native account versus contract caller, restrict[pair], unrestricted[caller] and output/reserve thresholds condition reward-hook invocation; these are not swap-denial rules and no MDX reward is promised.

Fee-supporting swaps compute input from pair balance minus reserve. Token-output supporting swaps check recipient balance increase; supporting token-to-BNB swaps unwrap the entire router WBNB balance. Fee-supporting liquidity removal transfers the entire router token balance; burn-accounting minimums do not guarantee net post-tax receipts.

Liquidity-add minimum checks are branch-dependent: an empty pair uses both desired amounts without separate minimum checks; nonempty branches check only the calculated optimal-side amount. No minimum LP-token output exists. Deadlines, slippage/tax behavior and recipients remain caller responsibilities.

sourceReview.nativeAsset: Four payable selected functions (addLiquidityETH and three BNB-input swaps) wrap BNB through immutable WBNB. Exact-output BNB-input swap and native liquidity addition refund excess BNB to caller. Native-output swaps and removals unwrap WBNB; receive accepts only WBNB.
sourceReview.swapMining: Both _swap and _swapSupportingFeeOnTransferTokens condition external ISwapMining.swap(caller,input,output,amountOut) on a nonzero configured hook. EOAs (tx.origin == msg.sender) invoke directly. Contract callers invoke for unrestricted pairs; restricted pairs additionally require unrestricted[caller] and both output-to-reserve ratios at or below getThreshold(pair). If ineligible the hook is skipped, not the pair swap. Threshold is per-pair when nonzero, otherwise default, scaled by 1e8/10000. Returned bool is ignored; external call failures still propagate. Current hook and reward eligibility are not asserted.
sourceReview.liquidity: addLiquidity can create a factory pair and mints to caller-selected recipient; minimum checks are branch-dependent and no minimum LP-output exists. Ordinary removal requires caller LP allowance, burns LP to explicit recipient (or router for native settlement), enforces both burn-accounting minimums and deadline. No signature capability is added.
sourceReview.feeOnTransfer: Supporting swaps use actual pair input balance-minus-reserve. Token-output supporting swaps compare recipient final-token balance increase with amountOutMin. Native-output supporting swaps instead use the entire router WBNB balance. Supporting removal sends the entire router token balance and checks burn-accounting minimums, not net taxed receipt. Ordinary exact-output paths do not solve token-tax accounting.
sourceReview.factoryAndCallbacks: Immutable factory supplies pairFor, creation, reserves and quotes, including token-aware getAmountIn/Out. Pair swaps always pass new bytes(0). No arbitrary executor, flash-swap callback or opaque multicall function appears in this deployed router ABI.

reviewSummary.nonFunctionEntries: One constructor, four events and one receive; none creates a capability.
reviewSummary.scope: Nine explicit exact-input/exact-output swaps and five ordinary non-permit liquidity actions at official BSC new_router. No old-router capability, mining administration, signature path, getter, arbitrary executor or callback is admitted.
